summary.text: A 31-year-old man with no past medical history presented with an extensive ulcerative black lesion on the posterior of the right thigh with right groin and neck swelling. He reported a thigh protuberance for one year that ulcerated after eight months. Examination showed a 15×15 cm lesion, right inguinal nodes and a 1.5 cm submandibular node.

Incisional biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry (S100 and Melan-A labeled) were consistent with amelanotic malignant melanoma. CT of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis confirmed metastatic lymphadenopathy of the right inguinal region.

He received eight cycles of Dartmouth chemotherapy with tamoxifen, with grade I neutropenia managed by GCSF and a 20% dose reduction, and had a dramatic response. Local radiotherapy to the thigh lesion and to inguinal and cervical nodes followed, after which examination was normal and the thigh lesion had healed.

About 15 months later he presented with nasal congestion, and imaging with biopsy showed metastatic melanoma of the paranasal sinuses. He underwent endonasal endoscopic excision with R2 resection, then radiotherapy of the nasal cavity, sinuses and skull base. He was followed for about seven years, with regression of the sinus tumor and no clinical disease.
